title: Contractor rapid onboard & knowledge-transfer playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical rapid-onboard playbook for short-term contractors, temps, and external consultants (<= 90 days). Focus is on minimizing ramp time while preserving team bandwidth and creating durable knowledge artifacts. The doc mixes an onboarding checklist, a minimal interview/risk rubric used for hiring brief, a 7/30 day activation schedule, KT session templates, and an exit handoff checklist.

Scope and assumptions:
- For contractors who will contribute to code, docs, or runbooks and need immediate operational access.
- Not for full-time ICs (we have a separate 30/60/90 onboarding).
- Assumes hiring manager or tech lead owns day-to-day onboarding tasks; People Ops facilitates checklist, access gating, and paperwork.
- Security: sensitive data access requires sponsor approval and an approved onboarding ticket.

High-level goals (success signals):
- First meaningful contribution within 5 working days (merge, doc update, task completion).
- Core system orientation completed within 3 days.
- KT artifacts (how-to notes, screen recordings, short runbooks) produced for each mission-critical area the contractor touches.

Pre-start (HR + hiring manager) 
- Offer accepted: send contractor welcome email with start date, point-of-contact, and onboarding agenda. (template: /templates/contractor-welcome)
- Create onboarding ticket in HR/IT queue with required tools and access. Tag SRE/security if infra access is needed.
- Sponsor (engineer) completes the "Access Justification" field and attaches required CLA/contract doc.
- Slack channel created and pinned as #eng-contract-<name>. Include manager, sponsor, and people-ops.
- Assign 1:1 buddy (not the sponsor) for first-week pairing.
- Draft 7-day activation plan and share with contractor before day 1.

Day 0 / Day 1 checklist (goal: move from zero to visible activity)
- People Ops: e-sign docs, background verification (if applicable), contractor badge/access.
- IT: laptop shipped (or provisioning window noted), VPN creds, SSO invite, MFA enrollment.
- Security: confirm least-privilege IAM role requested. Approve or escalate within 24h.
- Manager: kickoff meeting (30m) — intro, scope, deliverables, expected daily check-ins.
- Buddy: 1-hour dev environment pairing (get repo clone, basic run, tests).
- Contractor: confirm calendar entries for KT sessions and weekly 1:1.
- Quick wins: assign a small triaged task (low-risk) and a docs update task (README or setup doc).

Interview / risk rubric (for contractors) — keep short, hire fast but safe
- Core criteria (pass/fail guidance):
  - Relevant prior short-term engagement experience (0–2): prefer 1+ projects completed on similar stack.
  - Security/compliance sensitivity (0–2): high if touched PII or production infra. If 2, require 2-step approval.
  - Communication and async skills (0–2): essential for remote contractors.
  - Availability overlap (0–1): overlapping 4+ hours preferred for first two weeks.
- Red flags (immediate stop): inability to share minimal references, refuses to sign CLA/contract terms, or poor asynchronous response during trial task.
- Lightweight trial option: 4–8 hour paid trial task. Use for unknown candidates.

7-day activation schedule (template — adapt per role)
- Day 1: orientation, env setup, buddy pairing, first small task assigned.
- Day 2: KT session #1 — system overview + architecture diagram walkthrough (record).
- Day 3: Pair on ticket + review PR process, CI checks, and test runs.
- Day 4: KT session #2 — data flows and infra boundaries; provide list of runbooks to read.
- Day 5: Independent work on assigned ticket; submit draft PR and request buddy review.
- Week retrospective (30m) with manager: blockers, bandwidth ask, and commit for week 2.

30-day continuation checkpoints (if contract >30d)
- Deliverable review: are initial deliverables on track? Adjust scope if needed.
- KT artifacts produced: checklist of docs, short videos, playbooks added to central repo.
- Cost vs impact sanity check: manager + finance review. Consider conversion signals if frequently extended.

Knowledge transfer templates and prompts (for every KT session)
- Session title, owner, date, expected outcomes (2–3 bullets).
- Pre-read: 3 short links (read before session).
- Key flows to demo (step list).
- Failure modes + recovery steps (bullet list).
- What the contractor is allowed to change vs what is read-only.
- Open questions and follow-ups (assign owners and target dates).

Minimal KT artifact checklist (per domain touched)
- Short 8–12 step runbook (markdown) for the task the contractor completed.
- 5–10 minute screen recording of the end-to-end flow.
- Architecture blurb (1 paragraph) and diagram link.
- List of related Jira tickets and PRs.
- Contact map: who owns which component.

Manager/buddy playbook (notes to manager/buddy)
- Daily 20-minute pairing for first 3 days, then 3x/week for the rest of week 1.
- Do not give production write access until first PR review is merged and security sign-off done.
- Force the contractor to add one doc/update per task (improves bus factor).
- Use checklist-driven reviews: environment, tests, monitoring, runbooks.
- If contractor is blocked on approvals >48h, escalate to people-ops to unblock.

Exit and handoff checklist (last 5 working days)
- Inventory access: list every system and revoke schedule.
- Collect KT artifacts and upload to team "contractor-kt" folder. Confirm recording links.
- Final walkthrough: 60m with sponsor and doc owner to review artifacts and knowledge gaps.
- Close outstanding tickets or reassign with clear next steps.
- Deprovision tasks: HR to schedule access removal; manager to confirm removal.
- Optional offboard survey (2–4 questions) about onboarding friction.

Low-effort templates (copyable)
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — first steps and your week 1 plan" (include bullet points, Slack link, and calendar invites).
- KT session short template: "Title | Owner | Duration | Pre-reads | Outcome bullets | Record link (post)"
- Exit survey sample: "What slowed your ramp? What helped? One suggestion for manager?"

Open questions / to iterate (notes to self)
- Should we require mandatory 1-2 hour security orientation for any infra touching contractor? Might slow start but reduces risk.
- Trial task compensation: current practice unclear across hiring managers — need consistent policy.
- Can we automate some of the access justification approvals? Small wins for reducing 48h unblock.

Quick links (working folder and templates)
- Templates: /Drive/PeopleOps/templates/contractor-welcome, /Drive/PeopleOps/templates/kt-session
- Central KT folder: /Drive/Engineering/contractor-kt/ (ask infra for permission to write)
- Slack channel naming conventions and onboarding checklist in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PeopleOps/Contractor+Onboarding

Appendix: cheap checks for high-risk infra tasks
- Two-person review before any prod changes (one sponsor + one oncall).
- Limit blast radius: test accounts, reduced quotas, and feature flags.
- Short-lived creds where possible and automatic 48h expiration.

Notes to people-ops: this doc is intentionally pragmatic. Keep it lean, iterate from real contractor retros, and copy minimal templates into the HR onboarding flow.

Unresolved: need cross-team alignment on trial pay and access gating SLA. Will propose at next people-ops sync.
